samples.xml_description:
<module id="accu">
    <description>Implement a module to achieve serial input data accumulation output, input is 8bit data.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock input for synchronization.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal.</input>
        <input id="data_in" width_description="[7:0]">8-bit input data for addition.</input>
        <input id="valid_in">Input signal indicating readiness for new data.</input>
        <output id="valid_out">Output signal indicating when 4 input data accumulation is reached.</output>
        <output id="data_out" width_description="[9:0]">10-bit output data representing the accumulated sum.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="IDLE">0</parameter>
        <parameter id="DATA_IN">1</parameter>
        <parameter id="ACCUMULATE">2</parameter>
        <parameter id="OUTPUT">3</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="state" width_description="[1:0]">State register for FSM.</reg>
        <reg id="next_state" width_description="[1:0]">Next state register for FSM.</reg>
        <reg id="count" width_description="[1:0]">Count register for tracking input data.</reg>
        <reg id="sum" width_description="[9:0]">Accumulated sum register.</reg>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        The module operates in a finite state machine (FSM) manner, transitioning through four states: IDLE, DATA_IN, ACCUMULATE, and OUTPUT.
        - In the IDLE state, it waits for valid_in to be asserted to transition to DATA_IN.
        - In the DATA_IN state, it accumulates input data_in values until count reaches 3 (indicating 4 input values).
        - In the ACCUMULATE state, it calculates the output data_out by adding the accumulated sum to the current data_in.
        - In the OUTPUT state, it sets valid_out to indicate that the output is ready and transitions back to IDLE.
        The module resets all registers to their initial states when rst_n is low.
    </implementation>
</module>
